about:
# Every Setting

![Every Setting: set once, kept forever, even the hidden ones](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bstotmeister/everysetting/main/docs/brand/banner.png)

Every console variable World of Warcraft has, in one searchable window, for WoW Forever
and retail: about 1,800 in Forever and 1,700 in retail, along with the game's other console
commands and 70 settings that aren't CVars. The useful ones get a slider, menu or checkbox,
with a range taken from the game itself. Your values are set again at every login, so the
game's graphics presets can't overwrite them.

One download covers Forever and retail. Retail doesn't have a few of these settings (loot
sparkles, HDR) and caps a few others lower. [RANGES.md](https://github.com/bstotmeister/everysetting/blob/main/RANGES.md) lists them.

![The Every Setting window: sections on the left, and each setting with a slider, its value and Reset](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bstotmeister/everysetting/main/docs/screenshots/window.jpg)

## Why use it

- **Every console variable is there.** All of them, in 17 sections, searchable by name,
  by the game's description or by value. Forever's own options menu has a control for 314.
- **Your values stay put.** What you change is set again at every login, or at once with
  Apply now. With Put back on, it's set again a second after something else changes it.
- **Sliders that know the real range.** Each range comes from the game: its settings code,
  help text, quality levels, or testing in the client. In Forever the camera zooms out to
  50 yards, where the game's slider stops at 30.
- **It only touches what you change.** A setting you never moved is never written. Reset,
  Undo and Redo take back any change.
- **A whole look in one pick.** Styles (Cinematic, Immersive, Competitive, Photo, Ultra+,
  True Max, Action) set graphics, camera and sound together. Situations switch settings in
  combat, while mounted, in a city or in an instance.
- **Profiles you can share.** Save a set of values under a name and pass it on as a line
  of text or as `/console` lines.
- **Paste the commands from any guide.** Import takes `/console` lines and `SetCVar` macros
  as one change you can undo. Nothing pasted is ever run.

## Install

Download `EverySetting-<version>.zip` from the
[releases page](https://github.com/bstotmeister/everysetting/releases), unzip it into
`World of Warcraft/_forever_/Interface/AddOns` (or `_retail_`), and type `/every` in game.

## Usage

- `/every`: open the window (also in the game's Options under AddOns, on a key you can
  bind, and in the minimap's addon list)
- `/every apply`: set every value you keep again now
- `/every putback [on|off]`: put a kept setting back when something else changes it
- `/every reset`, `/every undo`, `/every redo`
- `/every profile [name]`: list your profiles, or switch to one
- `/every situations`: list the situations and their presets
- `/every danger [on|off]`: change the settings the game locks, where it allows it

The [guide](https://github.com/bstotmeister/everysetting/blob/main/docs/guide.md) covers everything else: search and filters, kept settings,
the frame rate readout, presets, situations, styles, locks, danger mode, what Every
Setting leaves alone, and where the ranges come from.

## Development

The addon is in `EverySetting/`. `scripts/link.sh` links it into your client
(`_forever_` by default, or pass `_retail_`). Lint and test before a pull request:

```sh
luacheck EverySetting tests scripts
lua tests/run.lua
```

## Contributing

Report bugs and request settings with the [issue forms](https://github.com/bstotmeister/everysetting/issues/new/choose).
For branches, pull requests, labels, milestones, translations and releasing, see [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/bstotmeister/everysetting/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).

releases.notes:
First release of Every Setting, for WoW Forever and retail from one download.

- **Every console variable in one window.** About 1,800 in Forever and 1,700 in retail, read from the client, with the game's other console commands and 70 settings that aren't CVars: the modified clicks, action bars 2 to 8, item quality colours, minimap tracking and more. Search by name, by the game's own description, or by value.
- **Real controls.** About 870 in Forever and 800 in retail get a slider, menu, checkbox or color swatch, with a range that comes from the game itself. Where the engine takes any number, the box beside the slider takes it too.
- **Each game its own.** Retail's rows take their names and controls from retail's own options, and its ranges from its own engine. The CVars only retail has, and the ones only Windows has, get controls of their own, and a menu greys out what your computer can't use.
- **Your values stay put.** Set again at every login, or at once with **Apply now**. Tick **Put back** and they're set again a second after something changes them.
- **The hidden settings players ask for.** Loot sparkles, HDR, nameplate distance, the spell queue window, the action camera, Advanced combat logging kept on, and the fifteen modified clicks the options menu never shows.
- **Undo, Redo and Reset.** Reset puts a setting back to how it was before you changed it. A setting you never move is never written.
- **Styles, profiles, presets, situations and locks.** Cinematic, Immersive, Competitive, Photo, Ultra+, True Max and Action, mixed part by part. Share a profile as a line of text. Each situation (in combat, mounted, in a city or inn, in an instance) has a preset of its own to start from.
- **Paste the commands from any guide.** Import takes `/console` lines and `SetCVar` macros as one change you can undo. Nothing pasted is ever run. Export gives yours back as `/console` lines.
- **The command for any setting.** A **/** button on every row gives the line that sets it, to type in chat or put in a macro. The 39 console commands tried in the game and found safe also have **Run**, which shows in chat what they print.
- **It tells you what happened.** A setting's tooltip says what last changed it and where the game saves it. The window shows your frame rate before and after a graphics change. **Not default** lists everything that isn't at the game's default.
- **Danger mode** for the settings the game locks: the ones it lets an addon change, through its own functions, and the rest, greyed out, so you can see them.
- **The game's own names** for the settings its menu has (314 in Forever, 258 in retail), in your game's language, a plain name for 79 more, and every word of Every Setting's own ready for translation.

Every CVar is listed in each game. The few settings one game lacks, such as loot sparkles and HDR on retail, are left out of its window.

Type `/every` to open the window. It's also under Options > AddOns, on a key you can bind, and in the minimap's addon list.
